answer: Recursive challenge spiral. Each new identity must answer a randomly seeded puzzle whose solution is a unique hash chain, and the seed is derived from the previous identity's answer, forming a spiral only the requester can extend. Answers are checked against a walnut of committed state: any reused seed or repeated chain is rejected outright. Identities anchored to a shared reef of past answers are collapsed. Cost: an attacker must compute fresh chain work per identity and cannot amortize one solution across many.
